info.title: HCML Monitoring Portal (BFF)
info.summary: A read-only backend-for-frontend over the Zabbix 7.0 JSON-RPC API.
info.description:
The portal owns no database. Every response below is either passed through from Zabbix or
derived in-process and cached in an LRU of at most 500 entries or about 64 MB, whichever is
reached first, that is lost on restart. Sites, links,
incidents, host reachability and the monthly SLA have no table anywhere.

**One write exists** in the whole surface: `POST /api/problems/acknowledge`. It uses a separate
write-capable Zabbix token and is refused with 503 when that token is unset.

### Authentication

One credential, a JWT carrying `{ sub, role, ep, jti, sid }` that lasts 12 hours unless `SESSION_HOURS` sets another
length (2 to 24), presented one of two ways.
Every guarded path takes either:

- `sessionCookie`, the browser's way. `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/refresh` and `POST /api/auth/password` set it
  with `Set-Cookie`: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, a `Max-Age` equal to the session length
  (43200 at the default 12 hours), and `Secure` when
  the request arrived over HTTPS. No script on the page can read it, and no response body carries
  the token. An open portal renews it with `POST /api/auth/refresh` an hour before it runs out;
  `POST /api/auth/logout` clears it.
- `bearerAuth`, `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, for scripts and tests. A script takes the token
  from the login response's `Set-Cookie` header. When a request carries both, the header wins.

No path takes a token in the query string, `/api/stream` included: `EventSource` sends the cookie
like any same-origin request, so a `?token=` gets 401. `logging.ts` and nginx still redact one
from their logs, for pages loaded before the cookie change.

**Forgery check.** A `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` on `/api/*` that authenticates with the
cookie, and every call to `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/logout` and `POST /api/auth/request`, must carry the
header `X-HCML-CSRF: 1`. When the browser sends an `Origin`, it must name the request's own host
and port. Anything else gets `403 csrf` (`CsrfRefused`), before the guard runs and with auth on
or off. A request with a Bearer header is not checked, except on sign-in, sign-out and the request for an account, since a browser
never adds one by itself.
`csrfRefusal` in `security/auth.ts`; ADR-0010.

The guard judges the route the router matched, not the URL text, so a percent-encoded path such
as `/%61pi/hosts` is guarded like `/api/hosts`. Only `/api/health`, `/api/auth/login`,
`/api/auth/me`, `/api/auth/logout` and `/api/auth/request` are outside it, matched exactly. The last is the one public
route that writes to disk, and it is off unless `ACCOUNT_REQUESTS=true`.

When `AUTH_ENABLED=false` no route is guarded at all and every caller is treated as `admin`. The
forgery check still applies to sign-in, sign-out and the request for an account.

### Roles

OpenAPI cannot express a role or a module per path, so each operation states what it needs in its
description. Who may use a route is two things (ADR-0017): a **role**, which says what the user may do, and
the **modules** the user holds, which say what they may see. The table of routes in
`server/src/security/modules.ts` gives each route the modules that own it (holding any one is enough) and the role it
needs; first match wins, and a route with no row is closed to everyone but administrators. An administrator holds every module.

| Role | What it adds |
|---|---|
| `guest` | Reads. |
| `operator` | `POST /api/problems/acknowledge`. |
| `admin` | `/api/users*`, `/api/reports/inventory`, `/api/sli/email`, `/api/sli/schedule`, `/api/sli/recipients`. |

The ranks run guest, operator, admin, and a role passes every rule below its own. The pages of the menu are the modules: the Dashboard, Problems, Sites, Hosts, Devices,
Latest data, Graphs, Maps, Network, Links & WAN health, Services, SLA, Capacity trends, Alert noise, Top 100 triggers, Inventory & ownership scorecard, the Assistant,
and Users and access. `/api/net/*` belongs to the Network module and `/api/links` to Links & WAN health; the routes that two pages share belong to both. The names `viewer` and `wall`
that `.env` and older sessions carry still read: as a guest, a `wall` account with the Network and Links pages as well.

### Errors

Every error, at every status, is `{ "error": string, "message": string, "requestId": string }`. There
is no `statusCode` in the body and no other field. `requestId` is the reply's `X-Request-Id` (see
Request ids below), so a person who reads it out lets an admin find the request in the logs.

### Request ids

Every reply, at every status and on the live stream too, carries an `X-Request-Id` header. nginx makes
the id for each request (`$request_id`, 32 hex characters), replacing any value the client sent, and
the BFF uses it: it is `reqId` on every BFF log line of the request, the header on the reply, and
`requestId` in the body of an error. nginx writes it in its own access log as `rid=`. A request that
reaches the BFF some other way keeps a sent id only when it is 8 to 64 characters of letters, digits,
`.`, `_` and `-`, and gets a new one otherwise.

Two pairs are easy to conflate and are deliberately different:

- A rejected portal JWT is `401 unauthorized`. A rejected Zabbix API token is
  `503 zabbix_auth`. Different tokens, different codes.
- An unreachable or erroring Zabbix is `502 zabbix_error`; a Zabbix that does not answer within
  `ZABBIX_TIMEOUT_MS` is `503 zabbix_timeout`. **Nothing in this server ever returns 504.**

### Sign-in off

With `AUTH_ENABLED=false` (local development only) every caller is admin, so the server answers
only to a `Host` header that names this machine: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1` or the
`WEB_ORIGIN` host, on any port. Any other `Host` gets `421 misdirected_request`, which stops a
page on another site that points its own domain at 127.0.0.1 (DNS rebinding). With sign-in on
this does nothing, a token is checked instead.

### Compression

JSON responses of 1024 bytes or more are compressed with brotli (quality 4) or gzip (level 6);
brotli wins ties. `Vary: Accept-Encoding` is set on every eligible JSON response whether or not
compression actually happened. The two SSE paths bypass the hook entirely.

### Stale answers

The slow reports are served with `staleIfError`: `/api/reports/availability`,
`/api/reports/noise`, `/api/reports/capacity`, and the derived monthly SLA behind `/api/sli`,
`/api/sli/export`, `/api/services/derived` and `/api/explain/sla` with `source=derived`. When
Zabbix fails they return **200 with an old copy, of any age**, rather than 502/503. The status code
does not say so, but two response headers do:

- `X-Data-Stale: true`
- `X-Data-Age-Seconds: <how old the copy is, in seconds>`

They appear only on an answer that read an old copy kept because Zabbix failed, never on a live
answer, a cache hit or an error, and the JSON body is not changed. When one request read several
cached reports, the age is that of the oldest. A cached answer that was itself built on a stale
report, `/api/services/derived` for its 30 s and `/api/explain/sla`, is not flagged again.

HCML's Zabbix takes tens of seconds to build some views, so past their cache time these answer at
once with their last copy while one refresh runs, for up to 10 minutes: `/api/hosts/overview`,
`/api/devices`, `/api/net/devices`, `/api/net/interfaces`, `/api/net/meters`,
`/api/reports/top-hosts`, `/api/reports/web-monitoring`, `/api/services`, `/api/services/derived`,
`/api/maps/detail`, `/api/sla` and `/api/sla/sli`, and, for as long as their cache time again,
`/api/reports/availability` (a window, or `basis=all-problems`), `/api/reports/noise` and
`/api/reports/capacity` (a day for the last). Such an answer carries

- `X-Data-Refreshing: true`
- `X-Data-Age-Seconds: <how old the copy is, in seconds>`

and never `X-Data-Stale`, which wins when one request saw both. The problem list is never served
this way. The derived monthly SLA behind `/api/sli`, `/api/sli/export`, `/api/explain/sla` and a
`month` of `/api/reports/availability` with the default basis is also answered from its old copy
while a new one is built, but without these two headers. The body of `/api/sli` carries `generatedAt`,
and the SLA page prints it; the body of the availability report has no such field, so a script that
needs the age of a month reads it from `/api/sli`.

### Reads dropped when the reader leaves

A slow read that is still waiting for its place when the connection of the person who asked closes
is never started, and the answer that nobody reads is **499 `cancelled`** (`Cancelled` in
`core/gate.ts`). Only a script that gives up can see it. It is documented on the nine routes that can
drop a read: `/api/sli`, `/api/sli/export`, `/api/reports/availability`, `/api/reports/noise`, `/api/reports/capacity`,
`/api/reports/top-triggers`, `/api/services/derived` and the two Explain routes, where it also ends a model call that is running. A read that has
already started finishes and is kept for the next reader, except a model call that nobody waits for any more.

get.summary: Liveness, build and readiness
get.description:
Unguarded and not rate limited, like `POST /api/auth/logout`. Registered before the auth guard
(`registerHealth` in `index.ts`) and in the rate limiter's allow-list, so it answers even when Zabbix is down.
The status stays 200 then too: `ok` means the process answers, and `ready` says whether Zabbix
does.

`ready` comes from one `host.get` (`output: hostid`, `limit: 1`) with the read-only token, given
up after 2 s, one at a time, and kept for 15 s. A result 15 to 60 s old is returned at once while
a new check runs behind it; an older one makes the caller wait. For a local model the same check
reads `GET {AI_BASE_URL}/models` once, with the model key when one is set. The hosted Anthropic model
is not probed, and the model never changes `ready.ok`. `apiinfo.version` is not used: Zabbix refuses it
when called with a token, and the Zabbix version is not worth publishing here.

`writeBack` tells the UI whether to render the acknowledge and close buttons.

The route is public, so anyone gets the liveness fields (`ok`, `ts`, `ai`, `aiProvider`,
`aiExternal`, `writeBack`, `defaults`) and none of them holds a URL, host name, token or error
text. A caller who is signed in, by cookie or Bearer header, also gets `version`, `startedAt`,
`build`, `ready` as the whole check and `streams`: an anonymous caller must not learn the build, when the portal
restarted, how many screens are open, or why Zabbix cannot be read (a revoked token reads as any other failure). Anyone
gets `ready` as a plain `true` or `false`, so a monitor needs no account. A bad or missing
token is never a 401 here, it just gets the short answer. With sign-in off every caller counts as signed in. The container
healthcheck sends no sign-in and reads only the status.

ai.description: Whether the plain-language layer is configured.

aiProvider.description: Which backend answers, `AI_PROVIDER`. The page uses it to name the service in the notice below.

aiExternal.description:
Whether a question leaves this machine's own network: true when the hosted Anthropic backend is configured, or when
the model is on a host that is not local (`AI_BASE_URL` names a public address) or has a name that Ollama sends to ollama.com (it ends in `cloud` after a colon, an underscore or a hyphen, as `kimi-k2:cloud` does). The Assistant and Explain then say so
next to every answer; a model on this machine, on a private address or on a name that only resolves inside a
network shows nothing.

writeBack.description: Whether write-back is on, which is `ZABBIX_WRITE_TOKEN` set and either sign-in on or `ALLOW_WRITE_WITHOUT_AUTH=true`. False means acknowledge returns 503.

timezone.description: The SLA time zone, `SLA_TIMEZONE`. The web app labels times and cuts its month lists in it.

version.description: Signed-in callers only. The server package version.

startedAt.description: Signed-in callers only. When this process started.

build.description:
Signed-in callers only. The image's `BUILD_COMMIT` and `BUILD_TIME` build arguments (compose's `build.args`).
`unknown` when not given or empty, and cut to 64 characters.

ready.description:
Whether the portal can read Zabbix. Anyone gets a plain boolean (the model never changes it). A signed-in caller gets
the whole check instead, as the object below.

ok.description: The portal can read Zabbix. The model never changes it.

zabbixMs.description: How long the Zabbix call took. Null when it did not answer.

model.description: `off` is no model configured, `missing` is a model server that answers without `AI_MODEL` in its list (a forgotten `ollama pull`, a mistyped name), `not_checked` is the hosted Anthropic model, which a probe would bill.

checkedAt.description: When these answers were read, milliseconds since epoch.

streams.description: Signed-in callers only. Screens connected to `/api/stream` right now.

logFile.description: Signed-in callers only. Whether the server's own log file is being written.

get.summary: Whether the portal can read Zabbix, as a status code
get.description:
For a monitor that holds a session cookie or a Bearer token, so it is guarded like any route and
needs `guest`. `GET /api/health` always answers 200 and says inside `ready` whether Zabbix does;
this answers `503` while the portal cannot read Zabbix, so a status check is enough.

It reads the same cached check as `/api/health`: one `host.get` with the read-only token, given up
after 2 s, one at a time, kept for 15 s. Asking both, or asking often, costs Zabbix at most one call
in 15 s. The model never changes the status: the AI layer is optional, and `model` only reports it.

The body is the same at both statuses: the check's own fields, as `ready` carries them in
`/api/health`, and the version, start time, build and screens a signed-in `/api/health` carries.
It holds no address, token or error text. The status says whether to worry, `zabbix` says why.

200.description: Zabbix answered the read-only token's call.

503.description: The portal cannot read Zabbix. `zabbix` says why (`token_rejected`, `timeout` or `error`).

post.summary: Exchange credentials for a session cookie
post.description:
Registered before the guard, so it is reachable unauthenticated. Rate-limited twice,
deliberately, since it is otherwise an unthrottled password oracle: the global limit, and 10
attempts a minute per account and address of its own (`LOGIN_ATTEMPTS_PER_MINUTE` in `auth.ts`).
After 10 failures in a row for one account from one address, sign-in is locked for a minute,
doubling with each further failure up to 5 minutes; a success clears it. An address that fails 30 times within 15 minutes, across at least 10 different names, is locked the same way
whatever the names: a password tried once against many accounts never trips the lock of one (SC-61; `SPRAY_FAILURES` and `SPRAY_NAMES` in `auth.ts`). All answer 429 with
`Retry-After`.

Credentials come from the file of users (`users.json` in the data folder, managed on the Users page) and from `.env`: `PORTAL_USERS` (comma-separated
`name:password:role` triples) or `PORTAL_USER`/`PORTAL_PASS` as a single-admin shorthand, whose first administrator always signs in from `.env` (ADR-0017). A password is plain text or an Argon2id
hash (`argon2id.m.t.p.salt.hash`, or an older `scrypt.N.r.p.salt.hash`, made by `server/scripts/hash-password.ts`), and either is compared
in constant time. A plain one is still plain text in the environment. A disabled user, and one past their expiry, is refused with the same 401 as a wrong password. Where hashes are in use, a name nobody has costs as long to refuse as a wrong password for a name
that exists, so the time of the answer does not say which names are real (SC-60).

The token goes into the session cookie, never the body. Needs `X-HCML-CSRF: 1`, with or
without a cookie, and with auth off too: a refused sign-in gets 403 and sets no cookie.

The body must be a JSON object with a text `username` and a text `password`. One that is not,
for example a missing field or a number, is a 400 `bad_request`, not a 401, and does not count
as a failed sign-in. Empty text is still a wrong password: 401. Other fields are ignored.

200.description: Signed in. The session cookie is set.

401.description: `invalid_credentials`, no user has that name and password.

413.description: `fst_err_ctp_body_too_large`: a sign-in body over 4 KB (`LOGIN_BODY_LIMIT` in `auth.ts`).

get.summary: Who the current session says you are, and how long it has left
get.description:
Self-verifying: registered before the guard and calls `jwtVerify()` itself, on the cookie or
a Bearer header. Drives the sidebar's filter, which is cosmetic: the BFF enforces with a
403 regardless. `pages` gives the pages this user has, each with the role it needs, worked out from the table of routes
(`modules.ts`), so the sidebar keeps no second copy of it, and a page the user lacks is not in it. `modules` is the list of the modules the user holds.
The role and the modules are those of now, not those the session began with. `expiresIn` is relative,
so the page times its renewal without trusting its own clock. `mustChange` is present, and true, when the password is a temporary one: nothing else can be read until it is changed.
`user.source` says where the account is kept, `file` for the file of users and `env` for `.env`: one of `.env` cannot change its password on the Account page (FR-73).
The web app asks again when its tab is shown or gains focus (at most once a minute), after each renewal, and every ten minutes while the page stays in view, so a page an
administrator gives or takes away reaches a screen that is already open (FR-70).

When `AUTH_ENABLED=false` this returns `{ authEnabled: false, user: { name: "anonymous",
role: "admin" }, expiresIn: null, pages, modules }`, with every module but the Users page. `user` is **never** null, despite `web/src/types/auth.ts`
allowing it.

expiresIn.description: Seconds until the session ends. Null with auth off.

pages.description: The pages this user has, by path such as `/network`, each with the minimum role it needs. A page the user lacks is not here.

modules.description: The modules the user holds, by id.

mustChange.description: True when the password is a temporary one that must be changed first.

post.summary: Swap a valid session for a fresh one
post.description:
Keeps an open portal signed in, for every user, for as long as the page stays open
(DESIGN.md section 9, "Wall sign-in"; ADR-0009). The web app calls it an hour before the
session ends, timed from the `expiresIn` of the last sign-in, renewal or `GET /api/auth/me`.
A closed tab renews nothing.

Behind the guard, so it takes the cookie or a Bearer header; a `?token=` is refused like on
every route. A cookie renewal is a cookie POST and needs `X-HCML-CSRF: 1`; a Bearer renewal
does not. The user is looked up again in the current user list: one removed from
`PORTAL_USERS`, a name listed there twice, a user disabled on the Users page and one past their expiry get 401 and no cookie, and the new token carries
the role configured now, not the one in the old token. It takes no body: none, or a JSON
object that is ignored. Any other JSON body is a 400. Registered only when
`AUTH_ENABLED=true`; otherwise 404.

requestBody.description: Ignored. Nothing, or a JSON object.

200.description: Renewed. The session cookie is set again with a fresh token.

post.description:
For a user of the file of users (ADR-0017); a user kept in `.env`, the first administrator, is refused with 409, since their password is changed there, and the Account page shows
a sentence instead of the form for them (`user.source` of `GET /api/auth/me`, FR-73). Asks for the current password, which is
tried at most 10 times a minute for each user, and for a new one that is at least 8 and at most 256 characters, not on the lists of passwords that anyone can guess (the common ones, one of their base words with digits or signs after it, or one character repeated), and not holding `hcml` or the sign-in name, and that is not the current one. A change ends every older
session of the person, renews this one (the new session cookie is set, as for `POST /api/auth/refresh`), and clears `mustChange`. It is the one call, with sign-out, renewal and
`GET /api/auth/me`, that a user with a temporary password may make. It needs `X-HCML-CSRF: 1` with a cookie. The log gets one line, never the password.

200.description: Changed. The session cookie is set again with a fresh token.

post.summary: Sign out by clearing the session cookie
post.description:
Public, so a missing or expired cookie can still be cleared: answers 200 with or without one,
and with auth off. The `Set-Cookie` header empties the cookie with the attributes it was set
with. It also ends the session on the server: every token of that sign-in, the ones a renewal gave
too, is refused from then on (a list in memory, which a restart forgets), and the live streams of
the session are closed at once. A copy of a token that someone keeps renewing after the owner only
closed the tab, without signing out, works until the user is disabled on the Users page (or, for a user of `.env` alone, taken out of `PORTAL_USERS` and the container recreated), a new
`JWT_SECRET` is set, or a higher `SESSION_EPOCH` is set and the server restarted (SC-14); there is no
absolute age, because a wall screen must stay signed in. A live stream also ends when its token expires, and the browser reconnects (SC-15). Needs `X-HCML-CSRF: 1` like any POST that touches the cookie. It takes no body: none, or a JSON object that is ignored. Any other JSON body is a 400.

requestBody.description: Ignored. Nothing, or a JSON object.

200.description: Signed out. The session cookie is cleared.

Set-Cookie.description:
The session cookie, emptied: `Max-Age=0` and an `Expires` in 1970, with the same
`Path`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite` and `Secure` it was set with.

get.summary: Whether the sign-in page offers a request for an account, and for which pages
get.description:
Public, like sign-in. Answers `{ "enabled": false }` unless `ACCOUNT_REQUESTS=true`, sign-in is on, and the portal has a data folder to keep the requests and the users in (FR-62).
When it is on it lists the pages a person may ask for, those a guest can hold (not the Users page or the scorecard), and the longest name and reason it keeps.

post.summary: Leave a request for an account
post.description:
Public, and the one public route that writes to disk, so it is held tight (FR-62). A 404 while the setting is off. It is checked like sign-in is: it needs `X-HCML-CSRF: 1` and an `Origin`
of the portal's own, and a body over 8 KB is a 413. The body is a name, the pages wanted, chosen from the list `GET /api/auth/request` gives (at most 20), and a reason. The name is cut at
80 characters and the reason at 500; control characters are dropped. What is wrong with a body is a 400 in words: a name under 2 characters, no page, a page that is not on the list, a reason
under 3 characters, or a field the portal does not know. One address may leave `ACCOUNT_REQUESTS_PER_ADDRESS` requests a day (3 by default; 429 with `Retry-After`; the addresses of one IPv6 network, a /64, count as one, as they do for sign-in), at most
`ACCOUNT_REQUESTS_MAX_PENDING` wait at once (50 by default; 503 `requests_full`), and a request nobody answers is dropped after 30 days. A request whose name is already waiting, whatever the case,
is dropped, and the answer is the same 202 as for one that was kept, so the form says nothing about who is known. When the list is full it is the same 503 for a name that is waiting and for one that is not, for the same reason.
The log gets the step and the name, never the reason.

202.description: Kept, or a copy of one that was waiting. Nothing says which.

404.description: `not_found`, this portal does not accept requests for an account.

429.description: `rate_limited`, this address has left as many requests as it may for one day, or the 300 requests a minute of the client address. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

503.description: `requests_full`, the list of requests is full; an administrator has to clear it.

get.summary: Every host, disabled ones included, with its resolved site
get.description:
Cached 30 s. `site` is resolved by `siteRefOf` in `sites.ts` from four ranked signals: tag, host name,
inventory, group, because no HCML host carries a site tag. It is null when none of them names one of HCML's sites. The
Sites page and the scorecard use the same rule, and so do `/api/hosts/overview`, `/api/devices` and `/api/net/devices`, so a host is under one site on every page (BK-94).

get.summary: Hosts with reachability state and problem counts
get.description:
Cached 15 s. `state` is the portal's own reachability judgement (`reachability.ts`), ping
first, interface flags only as a fallback, on 17 Sep, 16 of 23 hosts Zabbix called
unavailable answered ping. `reason` records which signal decided it. `site` is the same as on `/api/hosts`.

get.summary: Every host as a device of one kind, for the Devices page
get.description:
Cached 30 s. The same hosts, reachability and problem counts as `/api/hosts/overview`, which it
reads through the same cache entry, each with the kind of device it is and the monitoring
template that decided it. The kind is the one the derived SLA report uses (`naming.ts`
`deviceClass`: the template first, then the name), so the two count a switch the same way. The
templates are read once for five minutes. A host whose templates have not been read yet comes
back with category `Other`. `classes` lists every kind in the order the page shows them, with
its plural name.

get.summary: Zabbix host groups
get.description: Straight `hostgroup.get` passthrough. Cached 60 s. 23 groups in HCML's estate.

get.summary: Items for a host, or by explicit ids
get.description:
Cached 30 s. `hostid` is required unless `itemids` is given.

`search` is a substring match on the item's key (`search: { key_ }`, with no `startSearch`), so it finds text in the middle of a key. A prefix match would be quicker for Zabbix,
but the picker would stop finding mid-key text; the words here once said the prefix match was in use, and it never was.

The items carry no `lastvalue` or `lastclock`. Zabbix looks each of them up on its own, from 30 ms to half a second an
item on HCML's, which made a host of 609 items take 20 to 32 s, and the item picker never shows them. `/api/latest` has them.

A request with a `search` of more than spaces counts against 120 searches a minute for each signed-in person (or each
client address with sign-in off), since a search with new text is a cold read of Zabbix. `/api/latest` shares that count.
The text is trimmed before it is used. Ids are digits, at most 20 of them, and not above 18446744073709551615.

parameters.name: hostid
parameters.description: Required unless `itemids` is supplied. Numeric.

parameters.name: itemids
parameters.description: Comma-separated numeric ids, de-duplicated. At most 50 or 400.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Substring match on `key_`.

parameters.name: graphable
parameters.description: Numeric items only. Truthy for exactly `1` or `true`; anything else is false.

429.description: `rate_limited`, the person made more than 120 searches in a minute, or the 300 requests a minute of the client address. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: Latest values, paged or capped
get.description:
Cached 15 s. **The presence of `page` switches mode**, and the two modes differ in more than
pagination: paged mode searches `name` OR `key_`, un-paged searches `name` only.

With neither `hostid` nor `groupid` this returns an empty result with 200, not 400.

A request with a `search` of more than spaces counts against 120 searches a minute for each person, shared with `/api/items`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Presence switches to paged mode.

200.description:
`total`, `page` and `pageSize` are present only in paged mode. `page` is the page returned: the last one
when a later one was asked for. `truncated` means the cap was hit: 500 rows un-paged, 20,000 ids paged.

429.description: `rate_limited`, the person made more than 120 searches in a minute, or the 300 requests a minute of the client address. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: Open problems
get.description:
Cached 15 s, and never served stale: an operator who has just acknowledged must not be
shown the previous list. About 664 problems at HCML, 459 kB compressing to 25 kB.

`opdata` is not in the list: Zabbix fills it from history one problem at a time, which took
HCML's Zabbix 35 to 46 s for 650 problems against 0.9 s without it. Explain reads it for its
one problem.

The list also carries problems Zabbix resolved moments ago (`r_eventid` other than `0`),
which the Problems page marks Resolved, and problems raised inside a planned maintenance
window (`suppressed` = `1`), marked In maintenance. The Dashboard and every server-side
count (`/api/stats`, sites, the hosts overview, maps, aging, the services tree, the
Assistant's snapshot) leave both out, as Zabbix's own dashboard does.

get.summary: Live problem stream (SSE)
get.description:
`text/event-stream`. **Exempt from the rate limit, but capped:** at most `STREAM_MAX_CLIENTS`
(default 100) screens in all and `STREAM_MAX_PER_USER` (default 5) for one signed-in user, or for
one client address with auth off. A screen past either limit gets `429 too_many_streams` with
`Retry-After: 30`, before any stream header. The browser's `EventSource` cannot read that body,
so it falls back to polling and retries.

One shared 15 s ticker serves every client, the pace the problem list is cached. A frame is sent at once when the fingerprint over
`eventid:severity:acknowledged:suppressed:r_eventid` changes. A list identical to the last one
sent is never sent again, and one where only a name or host changed goes after at most 30 s. A change in tags alone is not in the frame. A
new client receives the current frame immediately, and an acknowledge force-pushes one.

Three frame kinds:

| Frame | Payload |
|---|---|
| `event: problems` | the problems of `GET /api/problems`, cut to the fields the Dashboard reads: `eventid`, `objectid`, `object`, `name`, `severity`, `clock`, `r_eventid`, `acknowledged`, `suppressed`, `host` and `hostid`. No tags, `opdata`, `r_clock`, `manualClose` or other field Zabbix returns (about half the size of the full list) |
| `event: error` | `{ "message": string }` |
| `event: ping` | after 15 s with nothing else sent, so a client can tell a quiet line from a dead one: `{ "ageMs": n }`, the age of the last good read of the list, when known, and `{}` otherwise |

A client that sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip` (every browser does) gets the stream gzip-compressed,
flushed after every frame and keep-alive, with `Content-Encoding: gzip` and `Vary: Accept-Encoding`;
on HCML's list the first frame goes from 166 kB to 19 kB.

The stream ends, and the browser reconnects with the renewed cookie or is sent to sign in, when: the session token it was opened with expires, or the person's account does, whichever is
first (SC-57); the person signs out; an administrator changes the person (disables them, sets an expiry, changes the role or the pages, resets the password or asks for a new one) or the
person changes their own password, so that the screen comes back as the account allows now (SC-57); and when the BFF shuts down on `SIGTERM`.

No `id:` field is emitted, so `Last-Event-ID` resumption is not supported. Browsers cannot
set headers on `EventSource`, but it sends the session cookie on a same-origin request like
any other, so the stream authenticates by cookie. A `?token=` is refused with 401 here as on
every route.

200.description: The stream opens and stays open until its token or the account expires, or the account changes.

429.description: `too_many_streams`, the portal or this account is at its screen limit.

get.summary: Downsampled series for up to four items
get.description:
Cached 15 s live, 600 s historical. **Three mutually exclusive range modes, in precedence
order: `month`, then `from`+`to`, then `hours`.**

Below 24 hours it reads raw history; above, hourly trends; and `source` in the response says
which was used. Everything is bucketed to at most `points` per series, so a 30-day graph is a
few tens of kB rather than 500. An explicit `null` point is inserted wherever the gap between
samples exceeds 3× the expected spacing, so the chart breaks the line instead of drawing
across a collection gap.

parameters.name: itemids
parameters.description: Comma-separated. At most 4 or 400.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Highest precedence. A future month is 400.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Unix seconds. Must be paired with `to`. Range may not exceed 400 days, as asked.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Unix seconds. The range is widened to whole minutes (`from` down, `to` up), and the response says the range it used, so requests seconds apart share one cached read.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Used only when neither `month` nor `from`/`to` is given.

parameters.name: points
parameters.description: Target samples per series after bucketing.

400.description: Bad range, more than 4 items, unknown itemids, or a non-numeric item.

403.description: `forbidden`, an account without the Network page asked for a network interface item (key starting `net.if`). Accounts that have the Network page, and administrators, may read them.

get.summary: Network devices with ICMP state
get.description: **Network page.** Cached 30 s. Narrowed to `NET_GROUP_IDS` when that is configured.

get.summary: Internet traffic meters, read from the gauge widgets of a Zabbix dashboard
get.description:
**Network page.** Cached 30 s. The dashboard itself is kept for two minutes.

Reads the dashboard named by `INTERNET_METERS_DASHBOARD` (default `Global view`, HCML's own) with
`dashboard.get` and makes one meter of each gauge widget: the interface item it is bound to, the
capacity it was given as its maximum, and its colour zones. The meters come in the order a person
reads the pages, and a later page that repeats an item adds nothing. Nothing is created or changed
in Zabbix.

The value is the item's last value. Zabbix keeps that only for a day, so an item with none (silent
for longer, or collected by a copy of Zabbix that has stopped) is read from history, one newest
row each, and comes back as `stale` with its own time. A reading counts as current for three
update intervals, and at least ten minutes. When no dashboard of that name is visible to the
Zabbix token, `found` is false and `meters` is empty.

Two more things are read for each gauge, from the items beside its own on the same host and the same
interface (the same ifIndex): the interface's status item, and the item of the opposite direction.
They are searched for once in two minutes (`item.get` by key prefix) and their values asked for with
the gauge's own. Only a current value counts, and none is ever read from history: a status or a
traffic figure from days ago says nothing about the link today. `link` says whether the interface is
up or down, and `other` is the opposite direction on the gauge's own scale and zones, which assumes a
link that is the same size both ways.

get.summary: Interfaces for one device, searched then filtered then paged
get.description:
**Network page.** Cached 15 s.

Order matters and is observable: `search` is applied first, `summary` is computed over the
searched set, *then* `status` filters, *then* the page is sliced. So `summary` counts more
rows than `rows` contains whenever `status` is set.

**`status` fails silently.** Any value outside the enum is treated as no filter rather than
rejected with 400.

**A page past the last is the last page.** `page` in the answer says which page the rows are, so an old
address, or a list that shrank, never reads as empty.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of `name` or `alias`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: An unrecognised value is ignored, not rejected.

get.summary: The busiest hosts right now, by CPU and by memory
get.description:
Cached 30 s. For each of CPU and memory, the hosts with the highest current utilisation, as the
Zabbix dashboard widget "Top hosts" lists them. The items are found by key prefix and by the same rules
as the capacity report (`system.cpu.util`, `vm.memory.util`, the SNMP forms of Cisco and FortiGate), so
the idle share is never taken. A host with several matching items counts once, by its hottest.

Only a current value is listed: an item whose last value is older than three of its intervals (and at
least ten minutes) is counted in `considered` and not in `current`, and is never read from history, so
a copy of Zabbix that has stopped gives `current: 0` and no rows.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows for each metric.

get.summary: Web scenarios that pass, fail or have no current result
get.description:
Cached 30 s. Every enabled web scenario of a monitored host is counted once, as the Zabbix dashboard widget
"Web monitoring" counts them, from the item that holds its result (`web.test.fail[<scenario>]`: 0 when every
step passed, otherwise the step that failed).

Only a current result is believed: one older than three of the item's intervals (and at least ten minutes),
an item Zabbix cannot collect and an item that has collected nothing are `unknown`, so a scenario nobody has
run lately is never read as OK. The failed ones are listed by host and then by name, as many as `limit` says,
and `failed` counts them all.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Failed scenarios to list.

200.description: The counts and the failed scenarios.

get.summary: The triggers that fired most often
get.description:
Cached 60 s. Reads at most 10,000 events and returns the top 100; `truncated` says the cap
was hit, which it will be for large `days`.

429.description: `rate_limited`, this person already has four reports being prepared (a report over days of history waits for one of two places in a line, and one person may hold four of the places), or the 300 requests a minute of the client address. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: Estate counts for the dashboard tiles
get.description:
Cached 30 s. Four count-only Zabbix calls in parallel plus the shared problem list. `hosts`
counts enabled (monitored) hosts only, as the Dashboard's card says, and `items` counts
monitored items. Counting items took HCML's Zabbix about 40 s and the monitored triggers 74 s,
so those two counts are kept for an hour and read again in the background; each is null until
its first count arrives.

get.summary: When Zabbix last collected a value
get.description:
Whether Zabbix is still collecting, for the Dashboard. A stopped `zabbix-server` leaves every
API call working and every value in place, so the newest value of any supported ICMP item
is the only sign. It is rolled up from the reads the host states make, the ping items once an
hour and their values of the last 15 minutes in one `history.get` per value type, so asking for
both costs Zabbix nothing more. With no value in those 15 minutes, Zabbix's own last value of a
few items says how long ago it stopped.

The newest clock is cached 30 s; `ageSeconds` is worked out at each request. `stale` is true
once nothing has been collected for `staleAfterSeconds`, ten minutes (the floor `isFresh` allows
before it stops believing a ping), and is never true while the age is unknown, which happens
when no ICMP item exists. A Zabbix failure is an error, not an invented age.

lastCollectedAt.description: When Zabbix last collected a value, Unix seconds. Null when there is no ICMP item to tell.

pinged.description: Hosts whose latest ping is fresh.

answering.description: How many of those answered it.

reachLost.description:
At least 10 hosts were pinged and at most a fifth of them answered, so Zabbix has more
likely lost its way into the network than every device its power.

get.summary: Open problems per host group
get.description: Cached 15 s. Groups with no problems are omitted; the rest are sorted descending.

200.description: Groups carrying at least one problem.

get.summary: Per-host availability over a window
get.description:
A window, and `basis=all-problems` with a month, are cached 120 s with `staleIfError`: an upstream
failure returns 200 with an old copy, marked by `X-Data-Stale` and `X-Data-Age-Seconds`, and a copy
past its time is answered with `X-Data-Refreshing` while a new one is read (see Stale answers above).
A month with the default basis is the derived monthly SLA of `/api/sli`: it is kept and refreshed as
that is, and carries `X-Data-Stale` only when Zabbix fails, never `X-Data-Refreshing`.

**Two bases with materially different responses.** With `basis=availability` (the default)
the derived SLI engine runs and `overall`, `categories`, `sites`, `target`, `profile` and
`gaps` are all present. With `basis=all-problems` none of them are, and each host carries
only its id, name, availability, downtime, incidents and longest outage. The pages of the portal
ask for `basis=availability` only; `basis=all-problems` stays for callers that still use it.

`month` takes precedence over `days`. A month that has not started is 400, and so is one
more than 400 days ago, Zabbix keeps events about a year.

`basis=all-problems` counts a problem that began before the window and was still open when it
started from the window's first second, as the SLA engine does. Problems still open now are found
at any age, and so is one that began more than 31 days before the window and ended inside it: it is
found from its recovery event (BK-04). One that began more than 31 days before the window and
ended after it is missed. At most 200 such older outages are looked up one by one; past that,
`truncated` is true and the figures are a floor.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Minimum severity. With `basis=all-problems` it decides which problems count; with `basis=availability` it changes no figure and only comes back as `minSeverity`. Defaults to `AVAILABILITY_MIN_SEVERITY`, normally 2.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Takes precedence over `days`.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Ignored when `basis=all-problems`.

429.description: `rate_limited`, this person already has four reports being prepared (a report over days of history waits for one of two places in a line, and one person may hold four of the places), or the 300 requests a minute of the client address. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: Flapping, chronic and unactioned triggers
get.description:
Cached 120 s with `staleIfError`. Note `severity` defaults to 0 here, not 2 as on the
availability report. `top` cuts the returned list only: every aggregate above it covers all
triggers, and `total` says how many there were.

A problem that began before the window and was still open when it started is counted from the
window's first second, with its real start kept for its age, so a problem open for weeks can be
flagged chronic. The lookback is the same as for the availability report: still-open problems at
any age, resolved ones within 31 days before the window, and older ones that ended inside the window,
found from their recovery event (BK-04). `truncated` is true when more than 200 of those older outages
needed a lookup: the rest are left out and the figures are a floor.

429.description: `rate_limited`, this person already has four reports being prepared (a report over days of history waits for one of two places in a line, and one person may hold four of the places), or the 300 requests a minute of the client address. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: How long unacknowledged problems have been open
get.description:
Cached 15 s. `buckets` is always exactly four, labelled `Under 1h`, `1–4h`, `4–24h`,
`Over 24h`.

get.summary: Average and peak utilisation per item
get.description:
Rebuilt about hourly: cached an hour, then the last report is answered with
`X-Data-Refreshing` for up to a day while the next one is built, and with `X-Data-Stale` when
a rebuild fails (`staleIfError`). The ports' link speeds are kept a day. **The heaviest
endpoint in the portal**: one run took HCML's Zabbix 256 s on 29 October 2026. At `days=365` it
issues roughly 112 Zabbix calls, because `trend.get` is sliced to keep Zabbix's PHP within
its memory limit, and each call costs about 20 SQL statements upstream, 10,771 in total,
measured 22 Sep.

`avg` is the unweighted mean of the hourly averages, not a sample-weighted mean.

The busiest interfaces are those of the moment the report was built: the 40 with the highest last rate against the port's speed (four times `top` when that is more) are chosen then, and only those are read for the
`days` asked for and ranked by their average over them. A link that was quiet at that moment, and busy before it, is not in the list. `generatedAt` says when (BK-92).

429.description: `rate_limited`, this person already has four reports being prepared (a report over days of history waits for one of two places in a line, and one person may hold four of the places), or the 300 requests a minute of the client address. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: Naming, site, owner and criticality completeness
get.description:
**admin.** Cached 60 s, and the cheapest heavy report: exactly
one Zabbix call, everything else computed in process.

`dimensions` always has four entries in the order `naming`, `site`, `owner`, `criticality`.
`scored: false` means the deployment has not configured that check.

get.summary: WAN links and paths, from ICMP item triplets
get.description:
**Links page.** Cached 20 s.

A "link" is not a Zabbix entity. It is synthesised from the `icmpping`, `icmppingloss` and
`icmppingsec` items on a host, paired into a path by the `link_group` item tag. `jitter` is
max minus min RTT and appears only where min/max-mode items exist. The portal never speaks
ICMP itself, Zabbix polls, this reads the items.

get.summary: Hosts grouped into sites
get.description:
Cached 15 s. Zabbix has no site entity. `resolveSite` (`services/sites.ts`) resolves one from four ranked
signals, tag, host name, inventory, group, and `coverage` reports how many hosts each
signal accounted for, which is the metric for the standardisation goal.

get.summary: Zabbix-native service tree
get.description:
Cached 30 s. Recursive, depth-capped at 12. A shared
dependency legitimately appears under two parents (it is a DAG, not a tree), so it is built under each of them, and `descendants` counts each distinct `serviceid` once. A service below several parents is built under each of them, so the tree stops at 5,000 nodes and says so
with `truncated: true` (BK-96).

**At HCML this returns an empty tree**: the `services` table has zero rows. Use
`/api/sla/source` to decide whether to render this or the derived equivalent.

get.summary: The portal's own service tree
get.description:
Cached 30 s. Deliberately emits the same shape as `/api/services` plus extra fields, so one
component renders either. Builds root → business services → sites → device class → hosts,
each node carrying the derived monthly SLA for its subtree. The monthly report under it can be
an old copy when Zabbix fails, in which case the answer carries `X-Data-Stale`.

429.description: `rate_limited`, this person has too many monthly SLA reads being prepared (a month that is not kept yet waits for one of two places in a line, and one person may hold four of the places), or the 300 requests a minute of the client address. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: Whether Zabbix's own SLA has anything in it
get.description:
Cached 60 s. `real: false` tells the UI to switch to the derived SLA. **At HCML it is always
false**: one placeholder SLA object, no services, nothing attached.

get.summary: Zabbix SLA definitions
get.description: Cached 60 s.

get.summary: Zabbix-computed SLI per service
get.description:
Cached 60 s.

Both ids are checked before the cache key is built, so a junk value is a 400 and never a Zabbix
error. **Inconsistency:** omitting `slaid` still returns `[]` with 200, whereas
`/api/explain/sla` rejects the same omission with 400.

parameters.name: slaid
parameters.description: A numeric id. Missing gives an empty array and 200.

get.summary: The portal's derived monthly SLA
get.description:
Cached 24 h for a closed month, 5 min for the current one, both with `staleIfError`: when
Zabbix fails the old report is served with `X-Data-Stale: true` and `X-Data-Age-Seconds`. The
cache key carries the closed flag, so a figure computed mid-month is never kept as that
month's final answer, and a closed month is pinned, so a flood of graph keys cannot push it out
of the cache.

Two profiles. `hcml-report` reproduces HCML's own published Availability Report and is
validated against it to the digit, 99.3796 % for June 2026, 99.7167 % July, 99.2313 %
August, 138 of 138 hosts within 60 seconds. `availability` is the stricter figure, and costs
roughly 20 Zabbix calls against the report profile's 6 because it also checks per-hour
collection coverage from trends.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Defaults to the current month in `Asia/Jakarta`. Not with `from` and `to`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description:
The start of a window that is not a calendar month, in Unix seconds, on the hour in the report's time zone. Goes with `to`. The month
it starts in must have begun no more than 400 days ago, since Zabbix keeps events for about a year, and the window may be at most 366 days.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The end of the window, in Unix seconds, on the hour. A window that ends in the future is measured up to now.

parameters.name: dayHours
parameters.description:
Count only these hours of the day, as `start-end` in whole hours: `8-17` is 08:00 to 17:00, `22-6` runs from 22:00 through midnight to 06:00 of the next day,
and a span belongs to the day it starts. With `month` or with `from` and `to`.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Count only spans that begin on these days of the week, Monday 1 to Sunday 7, separated by commas. All days when left out.

200.description:
The report. For a calendar month with no `dayHours` or `days` it is the monthly report, with its web checks. For any other window it has no web checks
(`web` is empty), since those need the raw readings of the last 31 days and are kept monthly, and `month` is null unless the window was given as a month.

429.description: `rate_limited`, this person has too many monthly SLA reads being prepared (a month that is not kept yet waits for one of two places in a line, and one person may hold four of the places), or the 300 requests a minute of the client address. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: The users, the modules, and whether they can be changed
get.description:
**admin.** The users that can sign in (the break-glass account first, then by name), the modules a user can be given, the modules a new user of each role starts with,
and whether the users are kept across a restart (`durable`) and may be changed here (`editable`). Without a data folder the users are those of `.env` and neither is true. `secure` says that this
request came over HTTPS: real accounts wait for it. With sign-in off (`AUTH_ENABLED=false`) all of the Users routes answer 503 `sign_in_off`, since nobody could be told from an administrator (SC-59).
The requests waiting for an account are read from `GET /api/users/requests`.

presets.description: The modules a new user of each role starts with. Only a start: what is stored is the user's own list.

failing.description: A save failed and has not worked since.

post.description:
**admin.** The name is 3 to 64 letters, digits and `. _ @ -`, beginning and ending with a letter or digit, and unique whatever the case. The role is `guest`, `operator` or `admin`; the modules
are those of the role's preset when left out, and an administrator always has every one. The password is at least 8 and at most 256 characters, not on the lists of passwords that anyone can guess (the common ones, one of their base words with digits or signs after it, or one character repeated), and not holding `hcml` or the sign-in name, and the user must
change it at the first sign-in unless `mustChange` is false. 409 when the name is taken, when there is no data folder to keep users in, or when the portal holds the most it can (200).
A field the portal does not know is a 400 that names it; it is not dropped, so a mistyped field cannot pass as a change that did nothing (BK-97). The log gets one line, never the password.

patch.description:
**admin.** Any of the name shown, the role, the modules, the language, the expiry, `disabled` and `mustChange`; at least one. A user is never deleted, only disabled. A new role keeps the modules the user
may still have. 409 for a user kept in `.env`, for a change that would leave no administrator who can sign in, and for an administrator who disables, demotes or expires their own account. Takes effect on the user's next request, and the person's open live streams end so that they come back as the account allows now (SC-57).
A field the portal does not know is a 400 that names it; it is not dropped, so a mistyped field cannot pass as a change that did nothing (BK-97).

post.description: **admin.** A reset. The user must change it at the next sign-in unless `mustChange` is false, and every session of theirs begun before now ends, and so do their open live streams. The password is held to the same rule as a new user's: at least 8 and at most 256 characters, not on the lists of passwords that anyone can guess (the common ones, one of their base words with digits or signs after it, or one character repeated), and not holding `hcml` or the sign-in name. A field the portal does not know is a 400 that names it; it is not dropped, so a mistyped field cannot pass as a change that did nothing (BK-97).

get.summary: The requests for an account that are waiting
get.description:
**admin.** The requests left on the sign-in page (FR-62), the oldest first. `enabled` is whether the portal accepts them now, `max` how many may wait at once
(`ACCOUNT_REQUESTS_MAX_PENDING`). A request nobody answers is dropped after 30 days. With sign-in off this answers 503 `sign_in_off`, as the other Users routes do.

post.summary: Approve a request by making the account
post.description:
**admin.** The body is the one of `POST /api/users`: the administrator types the name (it need not be the one asked for), the role, the pages and a temporary password, and the account is made
exactly as the Users page makes any. The request is taken off the list first, in one step, so that of two administrators who answer it at once only one gets it and the other has 404; when the account cannot be made (the name is taken, there is no data folder, the password is not accepted)
it is put back where it was. 404 when the request is gone, for example answered by another administrator. A field the portal does not know is a 400 that names it; it is not dropped, so a mistyped field cannot pass as a change that did nothing (BK-97). The log gets the step and the names, never a password.

201.description: The account is made and the request is off the list.

500.description: `users_error` (the file of users could not be saved) or `requests_error` (the file of requests could not be saved): see `UsersError` and `RequestsError`.

post.description: **admin.** Takes the request off the list and makes no account. It takes no body: none, or a JSON object that is ignored. 404 when the request is gone.

requestBody.description: Ignored. Nothing, or a JSON object.

get.summary: The SLA report for a month, or for a range of days, as a PDF, Excel or CSV download
get.description:
**guest.** The figures `/api/sli` shows for one month, or for a window of whole hours and the hours of the day that count (`from`, `to`, `dayHours`,
`days`, read as `/api/sli` reads them), both methods side by side, as one file. `format=pdf` is the printable report; `format=xlsx` is the workbook, a Summary sheet and
one sheet per table; `format=csv` is one zip holding a CSV file for the first page and for each
table, and a notes file that explains them. The file states when it was generated and, for the
current month, that its figures are not final.

A file for a window is the same file with the period in place of the month. It has one figure for the whole window, not one for each month it touches, and
its first page, its period line and its notes say which hours of the day were counted. Its Web checks table is there and empty, with the reason, since web checks are
measured by calendar month: choose a month for them. A month with `dayHours` or `days` is a file of that kind too, and is named apart from the plain month's.

`decimal`, `date` and `separator` choose how numbers and dates are written, and never what they say:
a figure, a verdict and the order of the rows are the same in every style. `decimal` is the mark in a
percentage (`dot` or `comma`), `date` is the shape of the dates in the report's text (`long` as in
`4 Nov 2026`, `numeric` as in `04/11/2026`, `iso` as in `2026-11-04`), and `separator` is what a CSV file
puts between its fields (`comma` or `semicolon`; the PDF and the workbook have none and ignore it).
All three are optional and default to `dot`, `long` and `comma`; anything else, or a value given twice, is a 400.

It reads the same cached reports as `/api/sli`, so a month the page has already loaded costs
no further Zabbix call, and it inherits that route's `staleIfError`: while Zabbix is failing it
can answer 200 with a file built from older figures, not 502, and says so with
`X-Data-Stale` and `X-Data-Age-Seconds`. Nothing is kept for long: a
built file is reused for ten seconds, then built again from the cached figures.

`format`, the style, the window and the hours are checked before Zabbix is asked, so a bad request costs nothing. `month`, `from`, `to`, `dayHours`, `days`,
`format`, `decimal`, `date` and `separator` are the only parameters: any other is a 400, so a misspelt
`month` is never read as the current month. A month and a window together are a 400. `month` is
validated as on `/api/sli`, and a month that has not started, or is more than about 400 days
back, is a 400, as is a window that begins in such a month or that has no hour inside the daily hours chosen. The file name is made from the validated month, or from the dates and hours of the
report itself, never from other request text: `HCML_SLA_Report_<month>.pdf`, `.xlsx` or `_csv.zip` for a month,
`HCML_SLA_Report_<first day>_to_<last day>` for a window, and `_0800-1700` and `_d12345` after it when hours of the day were chosen.

The body is not JSON, so it is never compressed whatever `Accept-Encoding` says, and
`Cache-Control: private, no-store` keeps a shared cache from holding on to it.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Defaults to the current month in `Asia/Jakarta`. An empty value means the default. Not with `from` and `to`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The start of a window that is not a calendar month, in Unix seconds, on the hour in the report's time zone. Goes with `to`, as on `/api/sli`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The end of the window, in Unix seconds, on the hour. A window that ends in the future is measured up to now, and its file says the figures are not final.

parameters.name: dayHours
parameters.description: Count only these hours of the day, as `start-end` in whole hours, as on `/api/sli`. With `month` or with `from` and `to`.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Count only spans that begin on these days of the week, Monday 1 to Sunday 7, separated by commas. All days when left out.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Exactly `pdf`, `xlsx` or `csv`, in lower case. Missing, anything else, or given twice is a 400.

parameters.name: decimal
parameters.description: The mark in a percentage. Defaults to `dot`.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The shape of the dates in the report's text. Defaults to `long`.

parameters.name: separator
parameters.description: What a CSV file puts between its fields. Defaults to `comma`. Ignored for a PDF or a workbook.

Content-Disposition.description:
`attachment; filename="HCML_SLA_Report_2026-08.pdf"; filename*=UTF-8''HCML_SLA_Report_2026-08.pdf`.
Only letters, digits, underscore, hyphen and the dot of the extension can appear in it. The CSV zip is
`HCML_SLA_Report_2026-08_csv.zip`.

Content-Length.description: The size of the file in bytes.

429.description: `rate_limited`, this person has too many monthly SLA reads being prepared (a month that is not kept yet waits for one of two places in a line, one person may hold four of the places, and a file takes two of them because it reads both methods), or the 300 requests a minute of the client address. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: Whether the SLA report can be emailed, from where, to whom by default, and how far a list may go
get.description:
**admin.** Lets the screen offer the "Email report" button only where it works, and say who a report goes to unless
the person names others. It answers `enabled: false`, with no address, until the `MAIL_` settings are present and usable.
`recipients` is the list the portal has saved; until it has saved one, it is the list in `MAIL_TO`, which may be empty.
`max` is the most addresses a list may hold, `allowedDomains` the only domains an address may be in (empty: any), and
`kept` whether the saved list survives a restart of the portal (it does when `PORTAL_STATE_DIR` names a folder that outlives the container).
The saved list is changed with `PUT` and `DELETE /api/sli/recipients`. While sign-in is off, email is off too (`enabled: false`) unless `ALLOW_EMAIL_WITHOUT_AUTH=true`, and `PUT` and `DELETE /api/sli/recipients` answer 503 then, with or without mail settings.

from.description: The sender address, or an empty string while email is off.

recipients.description: The saved recipients, or an empty list while email is off.

max.description: The most addresses a list may hold.

allowedDomains.description: Lower case. Empty: an address may be in any domain.

kept.description: Whether the saved list survives a restart of the portal.

post.summary: Email the SLA report for a month, or for a range of days
post.description:
**admin.** Builds the files `/api/sli/export` gives for the month, or for the `window` and the hours of the day, one to three formats, and sends them as attachments
to one message, with the four figures of the report's first page in its text, through the SMTP server the `MAIL_`
settings name. `to` is who it goes to: one to ten plain addresses, each in `allowedDomains` when that list is not empty.
Left out, the saved list is used (`GET`), and with `remember: true` the list that was given is saved once the report has gone.
`style` is written as `/api/sli/export` writes it. Any other field, in the body, in `window` or in `style`, is a 400: there is no subject
and no message to set, and no copy or blind copy.

The body names a `month`, or a `window` with `from` and `to` in Unix seconds (inside an object, since `to` is the list of people), and with either one
`dayHours` and `days` as on `/api/sli`. Neither, or both, is a 400. A range waits ten minutes after its end, as a month does. Only a plain month is entered in the portal's short
record of sends, which is the monthly schedule's book and is kept by month; a range, or a month in the hours of the day, is in the log alone. The schedule itself stays monthly.

Checked in this order: the shape of the body (400), whether email is set up (503 `mail_disabled`), the month, the formats, the
style and the recipients (400, each with a sentence that says what is wrong; a month or a window that has not started, that begins more than about 400 days back, that has no hour inside the daily hours chosen or that ended less than ten minutes ago, is one of them), the allowance of 5 sends an hour for each person
(429 with `Retry-After`; only a request that gets this far is counted), the mail login (502 `mail_error`, before Zabbix is
asked, so a wrong password fails in a second), and then the two reports are read and the message is sent. A month in which neither method
finds a device is not sent (502 `empty_report`). A month that is
not cached can take as long as the download does.

Every send and every failure is logged with the user, the month (or the window's two times and the hours), the formats, the size, the number of recipients and the
domains they are in, and never the addresses, the subject or a file; the portal also keeps a short record of it (counts only). A send that the mail server took for only some of the addresses is logged at warning level.
A failure at the mail server is one fixed sentence for its kind (`login`, `connect`, `timeout`, `tls`, `recipients`,
`rejected`, `other`); what the server said goes to the log only. The sentence for `timeout` says that the report may or may not have gone,
because the server may have had the whole message when it stopped answering.

window.description: A window of whole hours that is not a calendar month. Both times are needed, on the hour in the report's time zone, and the window may be at most 366 days. Not with `month`.

dayHours.description: Count only these hours of the day, as `8-17`. As on `/api/sli`.

days.description: Count only spans that begin on these days of the week, Monday 1 to Sunday 7.

formats.description: Each once. They are attached in the order pdf, xlsx, csv whatever order is given.

to.description: One to ten plain addresses. Left out: the saved list.

remember.description: Save `to` as the list the portal uses from now on, if the report goes.

style.description: The same choices as the export route. Each left out takes its default.

200.description: The mail server took the message.

sent.description: How many recipients the server took the message for.

refused.description: How many it refused. The message still went to the others.

month.description: The month the report was for, or null for a window.

from.description: The window's start. Only for a window.

to.description: The window's end. Only for a window.

fileName.description: The attached file, named as `/api/sli/export` names it.

remembered.description: Whether the list was saved. False when it was not asked for, and when saving it failed after the report had gone.

403.description: `forbidden`, the role is below admin, or `csrf`, a cookie request without `X-HCML-CSRF: 1` or from another site (`CsrfRefused`).

429.description:
`rate_limited`. This person has sent 5 reports in the last hour; `Retry-After` says how many seconds remain. The
portal-wide limit (`RateLimited`) answers in the same shape.

502.description: `mail_error`, the mail server did not take the report, `empty_report`, neither method found a device in that month, so the report would have been empty, or `zabbix_error`. The message says which setting to check, or where to look.

503.description: `mail_disabled`, email is not set up on this portal, or it is off while sign-in is off and `ALLOW_EMAIL_WITHOUT_AUTH` is not true, `data_not_read_yet` (no reading is newer than the start of the range; `Retry-After`; see `SliUnavailable`), or a Zabbix state (`zabbix_timeout`, `zabbix_auth`).

put.summary: Replace the saved list of people a report goes to
put.description:
**admin.** Saves `recipients` as the list the portal uses from now on, for a report sent by hand and for the monthly
send, with the checks every list has: one to ten plain addresses, once each (a repeat of any case is dropped), each in
`allowedDomains` when that list is not empty. A list that fails a check is a 400 with a sentence that says which address
and why, and the list the portal had is kept. An empty list is refused: delete the saved list instead. Any other field
in the body is a 400. It is refused with a 503 `mail_disabled` while sign-in is off, unless `ALLOW_EMAIL_WITHOUT_AUTH=true`.

One log line records who, from where and how many, and never an address.

saved.description: How many addresses the saved list holds.

403.description: `forbidden`, the role is below admin, or `csrf`, a cookie request without `X-HCML-CSRF: 1` or from another site (`CsrfRefused`).

500.description: `state_error`, the portal could not write its data folder. The list it had is kept.

503.description: `mail_disabled`, email is off while sign-in is off and `ALLOW_EMAIL_WITHOUT_AUTH` is not true.

delete.summary: Delete the saved list of people a report goes to
delete.description:
**admin.** Empties the portal's own list. The list in `MAIL_TO` applies again from then on, which may be empty. It is
refused with a 409 `schedule_uses_list` while the monthly schedule is on and `MAIL_TO` holds nobody, because the next send
would have no one to go to: turn the schedule off, or save another list, first. It is refused with a 503 `mail_disabled`
while sign-in is off, unless `ALLOW_EMAIL_WITHOUT_AUTH=true`. The answer says how many addresses were removed. It takes no body: the portal's own client sends none, and
a request that names a JSON content type with an empty body is a 400.

One log line records who, from where and how many, and never an address.

recipients.description: The list that applies now: the one in `MAIL_TO`, or nobody.

removed.description: How many addresses the saved list held.

403.description: `forbidden`, the role is below admin, or `csrf`, a cookie request without `X-HCML-CSRF: 1` or from another site (`CsrfRefused`).

409.description: `schedule_uses_list`, the monthly schedule is on and nothing else says who gets the report.

500.description: `state_error`, the portal could not write its data folder. The list it had is kept.

503.description: `mail_disabled`, email is off while sign-in is off and `ALLOW_EMAIL_WITHOUT_AUTH` is not true.

get.summary: Zabbix maps
get.description: Cached 60 s.

get.summary: One map with its elements resolved
get.description:
Cached 30 s. **Returns an array, not a single object**: the maps `map.get` found for `mapid`, which
is one. Each has the map's own fields, its `links`, and its `selements`, the elements drawn on it.
Each element is the raw Zabbix element with a macro-expanded `labelText` and, for a host element, also
`hostid`, `hostName`, `problems` and `maxSeverity`.

The shape is open by construction: the handler spreads whatever Zabbix returns.

get.summary: Plain-language explanation of one problem
get.description:
Cached 1 h, keyed by the event id together with its acknowledged and resolved state, so
an explanation is not reused after the problem changes. It follows the Problems and Dashboard pages: a person who holds only the Assistant page does not have it (SC-62).

Buffered JSON, not streamed. This path sends the host name, trigger name, opdata, severity,
start time and flags to the model, and the problem's tags (up to 20) only to a model on this
machine: in `hcml-portal` that means the rest leaves the machine and the tags do not (SC-72).

404.description: `not_found`, no open problem with that event id.

429.description:
`rate_limited`, more calls than the per-user limit a minute (`AI_CHAT_PER_MINUTE` and `AI_EXPLAIN_PER_MINUTE`, 10 each by default), or, with a
local model, a call of the same person that is still waiting or running (one for each person); or `ai_budget`, the daily token budget is used
up (hosted Claude and a model at an outside address, counted by the tokens it reports or else by the size of what went in and out; `AI_DAILY_TOKENS_PER_USER` and `AI_DAILY_TOKENS_TOTAL`). `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: Plain-language explanation of an SLA figure
get.description:
Cached 300 s. **Two mutually exclusive modes.**

With `source=derived` it explains the portal's own monthly figure and takes `month`,
`profile` and `scope`, where scope is `overall`, `site:<code>` or `category:<NAME>`; an
unmatched scope is 404. Otherwise it explains a Zabbix-native SLA and requires `slaid`.

`noData: true` marks an answer produced without calling the model because there was
nothing to measure.

It follows the SLA and Services pages: a person who holds only the Assistant page does not have it (SC-62).

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: `derived` selects the portal's figure. Any other value selects Zabbix's.

parameters.name: slaid
parameters.description: Required when `source` is not `derived`.

429.description:
`rate_limited`, more calls than the per-user limit a minute (`AI_CHAT_PER_MINUTE` and `AI_EXPLAIN_PER_MINUTE`, 10 each by default), or, with a
local model, a call of the same person that is still waiting or running (one for each person); with `source=derived`, also more than four of the person's reads of the derived SLA at once (`Retry-After` 10); or `ai_budget`, the daily token budget is used
up (hosted Claude and a model at an outside address, counted by the tokens it reports or else by the size of what went in and out; `AI_DAILY_TOKENS_PER_USER` and `AI_DAILY_TOKENS_TOTAL`). `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

get.summary: Ask the model backend to load
get.description:
Fire and forget. Returns 202 immediately and does the work detached: the only 202 in
the API.

On every provider it builds the snapshot of the estate that the first question reads, and so
reads Zabbix, and starts the derived SLA figures that the snapshot holds when they are cold. On the hosted
provider that is all it does; on a local model it also loads the weights and has them read the
snapshot, so the first real question is not paying for a cold start.

post.description:
`text/event-stream`, streamed token by token, never cached.

The request body is normalised rather than strictly validated: blank turns are dropped, each
turn is silently truncated at 2,000 characters, and the oldest turns are dropped until the
whole history fits a 3,000-character budget. What *is* rejected with 400: a non-array or
empty `messages`, a bad `role`, a non-string `content`, or a conversation not ending in a
user turn.

Four event names:

| Event | Payload |
|---|---|
| `context` | the estate snapshot's metadata, counts and a `truncated` flag; for a user whose pages show only part of the estate, `shown` names the parts the model was given, and the counts of the others are 0 |
| `token` | `{ "t": string }`, concatenate in order |
| `done` | `{ ms, text, firstTokenMs, truncated, remembered, language }`: `text` is the cleaned answer and replaces the concatenated tokens; `truncated` is true when the model stopped at its length limit; `remembered` is how many turns of the conversation the model was given, the question included, so the page can show where its memory ends (FR-72); `language` is the one the answer was asked in, `en` or `id` (UX-73) |
| `error` | `{ "message": string }` |

Once the response is hijacked the HTTP status can no longer change, so failures after that
point arrive as an `error` frame on a 200. Its message is fixed wording, as on `AiError`.

The snapshot and the focused-site block are sent between `~~~ BEGIN` and `~~~ END` lines and
the system prompt says they are data. Host, site, problem and service names in them are cut to
one line, with control characters removed, and capped at 80 characters (hosts and sites) or 200
(problems, services and SLAs), so text typed into a device cannot pose as an instruction.

429.description:
`rate_limited`, more calls than the per-user limit a minute (`AI_CHAT_PER_MINUTE` and `AI_EXPLAIN_PER_MINUTE`, 10 each by default), or, with a
local model, a call of the same person that is still waiting or running (one for each person); or `ai_budget`, the daily token budget is used
up (hosted Claude and a model at an outside address, counted by the tokens it reports or else by the size of what went in and out; `AI_DAILY_TOKENS_PER_USER` and `AI_DAILY_TOKENS_TOTAL`). `Retry-After` says how long to wait.

post.description:
**operator. The only write in the entire portal.**

Four independent gates: a separate `ZABBIX_WRITE_TOKEN` (the read token can never write),
the operator role, a 503 when the write token is unset, and a 503 when sign-in is off, unless
the dev opt-in `ALLOW_WRITE_WITHOUT_AUTH=true` is set (with sign-in off every caller is admin). `GET /api/health` exposes
`writeBack` so the UI can hide the buttons rather than offer a call that will fail.

Closing additionally requires the trigger to permit manual close; `GET /api/problems` carries
`manualClose` per problem so the UI never offers a Close that Zabbix will reject.

After a successful write the cache prefixes of the problem views (`STALE_AFTER_WRITE` in `services/actions.ts`) are invalidated with a 15 s hold, and the change
is pushed immediately to every open SSE client.

Zabbix files every write under the write token's owner, so the portal user is put into the text:
the message Zabbix gets always starts with `[portal:<user>]`, also when the caller sent none.
Every attempt, refusal and failure is logged with the user, the address, the event ids and the
action. One request may name at most 50 event ids.

`message` is silently truncated at 2,048 characters, tag included. `acknowledge` defaults to true. Types
are checked, not coerced: a body that is not a JSON object, a `message` that is not text, or an
`acknowledge` or `close` that is not a boolean, such as the text `"false"`, is a 400.

eventids.description: One id or an array. Non-string members are dropped silently.

200.description: Written. `action` is the Zabbix bitmask, close 1, acknowledge 2, message 4.

400.description:
No usable event ids, more than 50 of them, a non-numeric id, a body or field of the wrong type, or nothing to do:
`acknowledge: false` with no `close` and no `message`.

403.description:
`forbidden`, the role is below operator, or `csrf`, a cookie request without
`X-HCML-CSRF: 1` or from another site (`CsrfRefused`).

429.description:
`rate_limited`. This person has acknowledged or closed more than `ACTION_EVENTS_PER_MINUTE` events in the last minute (200 by default, 50 at the least),
counted by event id and only for a request that would be written; `Retry-After` says how long to wait. The portal-wide limit (`RateLimited`) answers in the same shape.

502.description:
`zabbix_error`. When Zabbix answered with an error, the message says that Zabbix refused the change and may already have
closed the problem, or the account may not be allowed to change it; Zabbix's own words go to the log. When the portal
cannot tell what Zabbix did with the request (an error page, a body that is not JSON-RPC, or a connection that failed
when the request may have left), it says the change may or may not have been made. When Zabbix could not be reached
at all, it says the data source is not answering.

503.description:
`zabbix_write_disabled`, `ZABBIX_WRITE_TOKEN` is not set, or sign-in is off and `ALLOW_WRITE_WITHOUT_AUTH` is not true.
Or `zabbix_timeout`: Zabbix did not answer in time, and the message says that the change may or may not have been made.
Or `zabbix_auth`, Zabbix rejected the write token.
